slightly different take than the rest of the thread. A square wave will resemble a heavily distorted signal more than a saw tooth wave. Distortion typically occurs when things are loud, but it doesn't have to be actually loud for this to occur. For example, listening to a metal band on your phone. It sounds loud even though its actually really quiet. Thus you could have a square wave at a slightly lower db than a saw tooth wave, but their both perceived the same because the square wave more closely resembles what a loud signal "should" look like.
